text:
Alex (Customer): Hey team, early this morning we started getting a bunch of 429s from the Redwood API. Traffic spiked for ~2 minutes, then started getting throttled. We're on the hosted plan. headers we see: `x-rd-burst-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 24`, `retry-after: 5`. Any advice?

Priya (Support): Thanks Alex — sorry about that. Can you paste: 1) the exact API endpoint you hit, 2) a short repro (curl loop is fine), and 3) whether this was a single client or many workers? Also is this during a scheduled job or a user-facing spike? :eyes:  

Alex (Customer): Endpoint is POST /v1/generate (text-gen). We have about 40 concurrent clients all ramping up quickly — a sudden promotional traffic spike. Repro snippet I used:  

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url} %{size_download}\n" -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\n  sleep 0.01\ndone\nwait\n```

When it happens we get a stream of 200s then a block of 429s with `x-rd-burst-remaining: 0`. First 429s start ~30s after the traffic spike.

Priya (Support): Helpful, thanks. Sounds like you're exhausting the account's burst bucket. Quick checklist: 
- Confirm account quota vs sustained rate (billing page).
- Check token-based rate headers (x-rate-limit-*) on successful responses to see the pre-spike remaining value.
- Short-term fix: client-side smoothing (cap concurrency + add randomized jitter/backoff).
- We can also temporarily bump burst credits if this was an expected one-off.

Sam (Eng-SRE): Adding context from infra side: our hosted tier enforces a smoothing policy to avoid noisy neighbors. Implementation is a leaky-bucket with two params: `burst_capacity` (tokens) and `regen_rate` (tokens/sec). If your parallelism consumes tokens faster than regen_rate*window, you hit 429s and headers show remaining=0. Typical regen_rate for hosted mid-tier is ~1 token/sec per 100 RPS equivalent. We also have a short smoothing window (60s) that amortizes small spikes.

Jordan (Eng-Infra): We saw your org id in the telemetry around 1862499965-1862500020. Quick notes: 
- You had sustained burst exhaustion: burst_capacity depleted in ~28s.
- The `retry-after` is advisory (5s) while bucket refills.
- We applied a transient safety cap to prevent a single org from absorbing excess capacity across a shard, which contributed to earlier 429 clustering. We've since reverted that cap for your shard at 1862500300 while we validate.

Alex (Customer): Appreciate the detail. Two questions: 1) how do burst credits differ from monthly quota for billing? 2) is there a way to smooth this automatically from our side without losing latency for normal requests?

Maya (Billing): Burst credits are primarily a serving-layer cushion — they don't change monthly billed quota but they influence short-term allowance. If you consistently exceed your plan's sustained throughput we may suggest moving to Dedicated or a different tier (or negotiate a higher sustained quota). No surprise billing for short bursts while within quota, but sustained overages could be billed or throttled depending on contract.

Priya (Support): For automatic smoothing client-side we recommend: 
1) Token-bucket client limiter: allow N concurrent tokens and a local refill matching expected sustained rate.
2) Exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (start at 200-500ms, cap at 10s).
3) Queue bursts at the edge (small worker pool) and prioritize interactive requests.

Sam (Eng-SRE): And server-side options: 
- We can increase burst_capacity for your org for a short window (manual uplift).
- If you expect regular spikes, Dedicated/reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and larger burst windows.
- We also recommend enabling caching for idempotent prompts and compacting prompts to reduce token consumption per call.

Alex (Customer): Could you share the headers to watch so we can instrument? I saw `x-rd-burst-remaining` and `retry-after`. Any others?

Jordan (Eng-Infra): Watch these: 
- `x-rd-burst-remaining`: remaining tokens in burst bucket
- `x-rd-burst-capacity`: max bucket size (rarely changed)
- `x-rate-limit-remaining` / `x-rate-limit-reset` for sustained caps
- `retry-after` when returning 429s

Priya (Support): I'll also open an internal ticket to track a short-term burst uplift. Alex, can you confirm the time window you'd like increased? We can do a scheduled uplift or a manual one-off.

Alex (Customer): If possible, a one-off bump for the 10:00-10:30 UTC promo. That would have covered it. Also any quick changes we can do today to reduce 429s?

Sam (Eng-SRE): Quick prod-safe steps: 
- Reduce per-client concurrency by 50% for the promo window.
- Implement client jitter/backoff (non-blocking path).
- If you use a request queue, add a short 100-300ms queue window to smooth peaks.

Priya (Support): Uplift request submitted. rate-limiter-bot will post in thread when done. Meanwhile, here is a tiny client-side snippet we recommend (Node):

```js
// naive limiter: allow 20 concurrent, queue others
const pLimit = require('p-limit');
const limit = pLimit(20);
async function send(req) {
  return limit(() => fetch('/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(req) }));
}

// on 429: retry with jitter
function backoff(attempt) {
  const base = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt, 10000);
  return base * (0.5 + Math.random() / 2);
}
```

rate-limiter-bot: Burst uplift applied to org 0123 for 1800s. New `x-rd-burst-capacity` = 600, regen_rate unchanged.

Alex (Customer): Confirmed — I see far fewer 429s in the next 10 minutes. The headers now show `x-rd-burst-remaining` dropping from 600 down. Thanks! :tada:

Jordan (Eng-Infra): Great. We'll follow up with a telemetry dump and recommend quota adjustment if spikes are frequent.

Maya (Billing): And I'll flag the uplift in billing so it doesn't accidentally trigger an overage review — we'll treat this as a CS-led transient uplift.

Priya (Support): Closing the loop: summary and action items: 
- Alex: add client-side limiter + jitter before next big promo.
- Eng: provided transient uplift + revert safety cap; will send telemetry.
- Billing: mark uplift as CS-managed.
- Support: follow up in 24h to ensure no recurrence.

Alex (Customer): Thanks all — smooth now. Will implement limiter and hit you if anything else crops up.
